history.gap: The unscrolled nav reserves width for the later "— OPEN DE DISCORD ↗" swap, so at rest DISCORD sits in an ~85px hole on either side while every other item is spaced ~28px; it reads as a broken flex gap, not a feature. At the bar the item keeps a single measured slot and the scrolled label grows from the dash without disturbing its neighbours (or the whole nav re-centres in one eased move). Beyond that, gold-small-caps-on-black-grain is a well-worn "private capital" costume; the header needs one element that is unmistakably this brand, not the category.
history.motion: No contact sheet supplied; between states the bar compacts, gains a gold hairline and swaps DISCORD for a dashed "OPEN DE DISCORD" — considered choreography, restrained, but the static reservation for it is visible.
history.verdict: B has the more distinctive atmosphere and a genuinely good vertical logotype, but it ships a struck-through mobile nav, low-contrast labels and no scrolled behaviour, which no jury forgives. A is the more generic idiom yet is built with real care — language switcher underline, scrolled hairline and label swap, tidy mobile — and loses points only for the gapped Discord slot and a look that belongs to the category rather than the brand.
